steps.phase: Read the frozen brief and surface unanswered choices
steps.title: Preserve the exact live problem brief
steps.content: LIVE BRIEF — Title: ‘Design an A/B Testing Framework for ML Models’. Slug: ‘design-an-a-b-testing-framework-for-ml-models’. Description: ‘Design an A/B testing and experimentation framework specifically for ML models in production, supporting traffic splitting, statistical analysis, multi-armed bandits, and automated experiment conclusion.’ Difficulty: Hard. Category: MLOps - Experimentation. Domain: aiml. Estimated time: 60-90 minutes. Requirements: ‘Route traffic between model variants’; ‘Implement statistically rigorous A/B tests’; ‘Support multi-armed bandit experiments’; ‘Track experiment metrics and outcomes’; ‘Handle interaction effects between experiments’; ‘Automate experiment conclusion decisions’; ‘Provide experiment dashboards and reports’; ‘Support feature flag-based model selection’. Constraints: ‘Traffic routing latency under 5ms’; ‘Statistical significance at p < 0.05’; ‘Support 50+ concurrent experiments’; ‘Handle metric corrections (novelty effect, etc.)’; ‘Consistent user assignment across sessions’. Hints: ‘Use consistent hashing for user bucketing’; ‘Implement sequential testing for early stopping’; ‘Use Bayesian methods for faster experiment conclusion’; ‘Implement CUPED for variance reduction’; ‘Use holdback groups for long-term measurement’; ‘Implement interleaving for ranking model comparison’. Tags: mlops, ab-testing, experimentation, statistics, traffic-routing, bandits. Companies: Netflix, Spotify, LinkedIn, Uber. This design reference preserves the problem statement and does not claim any target has been achieved. Numeric constraints are goals to validate against a measured workload; the hints are candidate techniques, not additional mandates.

steps.phase: Read the frozen brief and surface unanswered choices
steps.title: Identify choices the brief leaves open
steps.content: Ask which outcomes define success for each model use case, when outcome labels arrive, how corrected metrics are represented, which experiment populations may overlap, and whether an experiment uses fixed allocation or adaptive bandit allocation. Confirm what stable subject key is available to the router and which model variants and feature-flag rules are active. These are discovery questions, not new requirements or numeric targets.

steps.phase: Read the frozen brief and surface unanswered choices
steps.title: Separate the request path from experiment analysis
steps.content: Keep model selection on the serving request path and send exposure and outcome events to an asynchronous analysis path. Versioned experiment and feature-flag configuration controls assignment; analysis consumes recorded exposures and corrected outcomes, then writes experiment status and reports. Measure the routing target at the serving boundary and evaluate statistical conclusions from the selected experiment design.

steps.phase: Add the catalog-backed control and serving components
steps.title: Add the experiment console
steps.content: Provide an operator-facing surface to configure experiments and review their dashboards and reports. The console does not itself decide statistical significance; it displays the state produced by the analysis path.

component.label: Experiment Console
component.description: Operator UI for experiment configuration, dashboards, and reports.
component.highlightReason: The existing Web App catalog type represents the experiment administration and reporting surface.

properties.purpose: Create and inspect ML model experiments, feature-flag selections, analysis state, dashboards, and reports.

steps.phase: Add the catalog-backed control and serving components
steps.title: Represent production inference callers
steps.content: Model-serving callers send a stable subject key and request context so assignment can remain consistent across sessions. The exact identity contract is an integration question; do not substitute a transient session identifier when the brief requires user consistency.

component.label: Production ML Clients
component.description: Applications sending inference requests and later reporting observed outcomes.
component.highlightReason: A caller node makes the user-facing model-selection path and outcome source explicit.

properties.purpose: Send inference requests with a stable experiment subject key and emit outcome events when the product has an observed result.

steps.phase: Add the catalog-backed control and serving components
steps.title: Add the experiment control API
steps.content: Accept experiment definitions and feature-flag changes through a control API. Validate the configuration and persist its version before making it available to the request router; keep control-plane work off the per-inference decision path.

component.label: Experiment Control API
component.description: Validates and publishes experiment and feature-flag configuration.
component.highlightReason: The catalog API Gateway provides the existing control-plane API type.

properties.purpose: Validate experiment lifecycle and model-selection changes, then publish versioned configuration through the control plane.

steps.phase: Add the catalog-backed control and serving components
steps.title: Represent versioned feature-flag rules
steps.content: The catalog has no dedicated feature-flag component. Use its existing Configuration Management type for versioned model-selection flags, experiment allocation rules, layer membership, and the snapshot consumed by routing. Publish each revision atomically; routers keep a local last-known-good snapshot so a config outage does not add a remote lookup to the sub-5ms request path.

component.label: Versioned Experiment and Feature Flags
component.description: Atomic, versioned model flags, allocation weights, and experiment-layer rules distributed as a last-known-good router snapshot.
component.highlightReason: Configuration Management is the closest existing catalog type for versioned feature-flag rules.

properties.purpose: Publish atomic versioned flags, variant weights, and experiment-layer membership. Routers consume a local last-known-good snapshot and record its version with each assignment, avoiding a synchronous control-plane lookup on the inference path.

steps.phase: Add the catalog-backed control and serving components
steps.title: Keep experiment definitions and lifecycle state
steps.content: Persist experiment identity, model variants, allocation policy, primary metric definitions, the pre-registered statistical plan, interaction layer or mutual-exclusion group, and conclusion state. Reject conflicting assignments within a layer while permitting independent layers to run concurrently; the brief does not prescribe a storage engine or partition strategy.

component.label: Experiment Registry
component.description: Pre-registered experiment metrics and test plans, variant allocation, interaction layers, and lifecycle/conclusion state.
component.highlightReason: The existing Experiment Tracking component represents the experiment lifecycle and metadata role.

properties.purpose: Persist variants, randomization unit, primary metrics, test family and stopping plan, alpha policy, interaction layer/mutual-exclusion group, and lifecycle state. Reject incompatible concurrent assignments within a layer; pass the versioned policy to routing and analysis so both use the same experiment definition.

steps.phase: Add the catalog-backed control and serving components
steps.title: Route each request using a stable assignment
steps.content: Resolve active flags and layer eligibility from an in-memory atomic snapshot, then use a stable subject key and consistent hashing to route to the selected variant. Persist the first assignment for an enrolled subject so later bandit weight revisions do not move that subject between variants; use last-known-good configuration during a control-plane outage and keep analysis off the request path.

component.label: Experiment Traffic Router
component.description: Sub-5ms local-snapshot routing with stable subject hashing, layer conflict checks, sticky assignments, and last-known-good fallback.
component.highlightReason: The existing Load Balancer supports traffic selection and stickiness; assignment semantics are stated explicitly in its purpose.

properties.purpose: Within the supplied sub-5ms target, evaluate an atomically swapped local last-known-good config snapshot, resolve the subject's experiment layer, and consistently hash a stable subject key with experiment ID and assignment epoch. Persist the initial variant assignment so config or bandit weight changes do not silently move an enrolled subject; never synchronously call analysis or storage on the inference path.
properties.algorithm: Consistent hashing by stable experiment subject key

steps.phase: Add the catalog-backed control and serving components
steps.title: Add the first model variant
steps.content: Represent one configured model variant behind the serving boundary. Its model identity and deployment details come from the experiment definition; the live brief does not name a serving platform or instance count.

component.label: Model Variant A
component.highlightReason: The catalog includes a dedicated Model Serving type for production variants.

properties.purpose: Serve the model version selected by the experiment traffic router.

steps.phase: Add the catalog-backed control and serving components
steps.title: Add another selectable model variant
steps.content: A second serving target makes the traffic-splitting path concrete. The same component type can represent additional variants without inventing a new catalog node type.

component.label: Model Variant B
component.description: A second selectable production model version.
component.highlightReason: A second existing Model Serving node represents the alternative arm in the experiment.

properties.purpose: Serve the alternative model version selected by the experiment traffic router.

steps.phase: Add the catalog-backed control and serving components
steps.title: Buffer assignment, exposure, and outcome events
steps.content: Record assignment separately from actual exposure. Every immutable event carries event_id, exposure_id, experiment_id, variant_id, subject hash, config/test-plan version, event time, and (for outcomes) metric_id and revision so late corrections update the original evidence rather than create another exposure.

component.label: Experiment Event Stream
component.description: Durable assignment/exposure/outcome stream with stable event and exposure IDs, config version, metric identity, and correction revision.
component.highlightReason: The catalog Message Broker provides the existing durable event boundary.

properties.purpose: Durably buffer immutable assignment, actual-exposure, outcome, and correction events. Include event_id, exposure_id, experiment_id, variant_id, pseudonymous subject hash, config/test-plan version, event time, metric_id, and correction revision; preserve assignment versus exposure as distinct facts.

steps.phase: Add the catalog-backed control and serving components
steps.title: Normalize outcomes and apply metric corrections
steps.content: Join each outcome to its original exposure using exposure_id plus experiment, variant, and metric identity. Deduplicate at-least-once delivery by event_id; apply corrections as idempotent upserts keyed by exposure_id and metric_id/revision, recompute affected aggregates, and keep results provisional until the correction watermark is reconciled.

component.label: Outcome and Correction Processor
component.description: Idempotently joins outcomes to exposures, deduplicates events, and replaces corrected metric revisions before analysis.
component.highlightReason: The existing Stream Processor type fits ordered event aggregation and stateful correction handling.

properties.purpose: Deduplicate at-least-once records by event_id and join outcome/correction records to the original exposure using exposure_id, experiment_id, variant_id, and metric_id. Upsert the latest correction revision instead of counting it as a new observation, recompute affected aggregates, and emit a settled-through watermark plus correction status for statistical analysis.

steps.phase: Add the catalog-backed control and serving components
steps.title: Evaluate experiments and conclusion policies
steps.content: Apply the pre-registered test family to reconciled metrics: use a two-sided Welch test for continuous outcomes and a two-proportion test for binary outcomes; use Holm adjustment across declared primary comparisons. For planned interim looks, use an O'Brien-Fleming alpha-spending boundary to control family-wise alpha at 0.05 rather than stopping on repeated unadjusted p-values. Model declared interaction terms or analyze only compatible layers, and keep Bayesian bandit allocation decisions separate from frequentist A/B significance conclusions.

component.label: Experiment Analysis and Decision Engine
component.description: Pre-registered Welch/two-proportion tests, Holm-adjusted primary comparisons, sequential alpha-spending, interaction analysis, and separate bandit decisions.
component.highlightReason: The existing Analytics component covers statistical evaluation and experiment outcome computation.

properties.purpose: Evaluate only reconciled exposure/outcome evidence under the versioned pre-registered plan: two-sided Welch tests for continuous outcomes, two-proportion tests for binary outcomes, Holm adjustment across declared primary comparisons, and O'Brien-Fleming alpha-spending for planned sequential looks with family-wise alpha at 0.05. Include declared interaction terms or restrict inference to compatible layers; block a final claim while corrections are unsettled. Keep Bayesian bandit allocation/posterior decisions separate from p<0.05 A/B conclusions, and persist the method and evidence used.

steps.phase: Add the catalog-backed control and serving components
steps.title: Persist metric evidence and decisions
steps.content: Store experiment summaries, the test-plan/config version, corrected-data watermark, metric estimates and confidence intervals, raw and adjusted p-values, sample counts, interaction policy, and conclusion status so reports are reproducible and distinguish significant, inconclusive, and awaiting-correction results. Retention and database choice are not specified by the live brief.

component.label: Experiment Results Store
component.description: Queryable corrected metric evidence, plan/config versions, confidence intervals, adjusted significance results, and reevaluation state.
component.highlightReason: The existing Database type represents durable queryable experiment results.

properties.purpose: Persist metric estimates, confidence intervals, sample counts, raw/adjusted p-values, test family and plan version, assignment/config version, corrected-data watermark, interaction policy, and conclusion rationale. Expose significant, inconclusive, and awaiting-correction states separately so reports can be reproduced from the exact evidence.

steps.phase: Connect assignment, serving, and metrics paths
steps.title: Connect the console to the control API
steps.content: Send experiment edits and report queries through the control API so configuration changes have a validated control-plane boundary.

connection.label: Experiment edits and report queries
connection.description: The console submits validated control-plane changes and requests experiment reports.

steps.phase: Connect assignment, serving, and metrics paths
steps.title: Persist experiment definitions
steps.content: Store each experiment definition and lifecycle transition before its rules are published to serving routers.

connection.label: Versioned experiment definitions
connection.description: Persist variants, metrics, interaction policy, allocation mode, and lifecycle state.

steps.phase: Connect assignment, serving, and metrics paths
steps.title: Publish feature-flag configuration
steps.content: The control API publishes validated, versioned model-selection rules to configuration management; request routing consumes a prepared snapshot rather than waiting on control-plane edits.

connection.label: Validated versioned flags
connection.description: Publish the feature-flag and experiment allocation snapshot used by request routing.

steps.phase: Connect assignment, serving, and metrics paths
steps.title: Bind allocation rules to experiment state
steps.content: Keep the active experiment definition and its model-selection allocation aligned with the versioned feature-flag snapshot.

connection.label: Experiment allocation policy
connection.description: Publish the experiment's versioned variant weights, stable assignment epoch, interaction layer, and mutual-exclusion group together so routing can reject conflicts without querying the registry on the hot path.

steps.phase: Connect assignment, serving, and metrics paths
steps.title: Deliver the active selection snapshot to routing
steps.content: Make the current feature flags and assignment policy available to the router while preserving the configuration version used for each decision.

connection.label: Versioned model-selection rules
connection.description: Deliver an atomic config revision with layer rules and assignment epoch; the router uses its local last-known-good copy and records the revision for every decision.

steps.phase: Connect assignment, serving, and metrics paths
steps.title: Make active variants available to the router
steps.content: The router needs the experiment identity and eligible variants corresponding to the allocation rules it evaluates.

connection.label: Active experiment and variants
connection.description: Provide eligible variants, subject population, layer/mutual-exclusion membership, and assignment epoch; the router rejects conflicting assignments within a layer while preserving independent concurrent layers.

steps.phase: Connect assignment, serving, and metrics paths
steps.title: Send inference traffic through experiment assignment
steps.content: Route model requests through the experiment router so feature flags and stable subject bucketing choose the variant before inference.

connection.label: Inference request and stable subject key
connection.description: The caller supplies the subject identity needed for consistent cross-session assignment.

steps.phase: Connect assignment, serving, and metrics paths
steps.title: Route requests to variant A
steps.content: The router selects this model endpoint only when the active feature flag and experiment allocation assign the request to variant A.

connection.label: Assigned inference request
connection.description: Forward requests assigned to model variant A.

steps.phase: Connect assignment, serving, and metrics paths
steps.title: Route requests to variant B
steps.content: The second route makes the alternative model arm explicit; allocation proportions remain experiment configuration, not invented fixed values.

connection.label: Assigned inference request
connection.description: Forward requests assigned to model variant B according to the active allocation policy.

steps.phase: Connect assignment, serving, and metrics paths
steps.title: Return variant A inference results
steps.content: Return the prediction and variant identity to the router so request and exposure records can be associated with the assignment.

connection.label: Prediction and variant identity
connection.description: Return the selected model's response with identifiers needed for exposure attribution.

steps.phase: Connect assignment, serving, and metrics paths
steps.title: Return variant B inference results
steps.content: Keep response attribution consistent across model variants so later outcomes can be compared under the same experiment definition.

connection.label: Prediction and variant identity
connection.description: Return the selected model's response with identifiers needed for exposure attribution.

steps.phase: Connect assignment, serving, and metrics paths
steps.title: Record assignment and actual exposure
steps.content: Emit the experiment, variant, assignment, and exposure identifiers after routing so analysis can distinguish assigned traffic from actual model exposure.

connection.label: Assignment and exposure events
connection.description: Record assignment and actual exposure separately with event_id, exposure_id, experiment/variant IDs, subject hash, config version, and event time for unbiased attribution.

steps.phase: Connect assignment, serving, and metrics paths
steps.title: Send observed outcomes for analysis
steps.content: Outcomes can arrive after inference and may later be corrected. Preserve the experiment and exposure identity needed to associate them with the original assignment.

connection.label: Observed outcome and correction events
connection.description: Deliver each outcome with event_id, original exposure_id, experiment/variant, metric_id, event time, and correction revision so updates can replace prior contributions idempotently.

steps.phase: Connect assignment, serving, and metrics paths
steps.title: Process experiment events
steps.content: Consume assignment, exposure, outcome, and correction events in the analysis pipeline while retaining the event identities needed for reconciliation.

connection.label: Experiment and metric events
connection.description: Deliver at-least-once event records; the processor deduplicates by event_id and uses exposure_id plus metric/revision identity for idempotent joins and correction upserts.

steps.phase: Connect assignment, serving, and metrics paths
steps.title: Send reconciled metrics to statistical analysis
steps.content: Pass attributed and correction-aware observations to the decision engine so experiment statistics reflect the current metric evidence.

connection.label: Attributed corrected metric inputs
connection.description: Provide deduplicated, correction-merged metric aggregates with a settled-through watermark; do not emit a final significance decision while corrections remain unresolved.

steps.phase: Connect assignment, serving, and metrics paths
steps.title: Evaluate outcomes against experiment definitions
steps.content: Use the experiment's metric definitions, allocation mode, and interaction metadata when interpreting the event-derived outcomes.

connection.label: Metrics, allocation, and interaction plan
connection.description: Supply the pre-registered primary metrics, test family, alpha/stopping plan, variant allocation, and interaction layer so inference matches the launched experiment.

steps.phase: Connect assignment, serving, and metrics paths
steps.title: Persist analysis results and evidence state
steps.content: Persist the analysis outputs and correction-aware state that support dashboards, reports, and auditable conclusion decisions.

connection.label: Metric evidence and analysis results
connection.description: Store estimates, confidence intervals, sample counts, raw and Holm-adjusted p-values, sequential look/alpha boundary, input watermark, plan/config versions, and significant/inconclusive/pending-correction status.

steps.phase: Connect assignment, serving, and metrics paths
steps.title: Record automated experiment conclusions
steps.content: Write a conclusion and its evidence state back to the experiment lifecycle record; a later metric correction can trigger reevaluation rather than leaving a stale conclusion unmarked.

connection.label: Conclusion and reevaluation state
connection.description: Update the experiment lifecycle with the conclusion status and whether corrected evidence requires reevaluation.

steps.phase: Connect assignment, serving, and metrics paths
steps.title: Feed adaptive allocation updates to configuration
steps.content: For experiments using a bandit policy, publish its current allocation decision through versioned configuration so the router can apply it consistently and the allocation history remains attributable.

connection.label: Versioned bandit allocation update
connection.description: Publish bandit weight changes as an atomic versioned snapshot for new enrollment while preserving persisted variant assignments for already enrolled subjects; keep posterior decisions distinct from p<0.05 A/B conclusions.

steps.phase: Connect assignment, serving, and metrics paths
steps.title: Make reports available through the control API
steps.content: Expose persisted metric state and conclusions to the experiment console through the control API.

connection.label: Query experiment reports
connection.description: Read stored outcomes, correction state, and conclusion evidence for authorized report responses.

steps.phase: Connect assignment, serving, and metrics paths
steps.title: Return dashboards and reports to the console
steps.content: Return report data and lifecycle state to the console without coupling the dashboard to the live inference path.

connection.label: Dashboard and report response
connection.description: Deliver experiment dashboards, reports, and current conclusion state to the operator UI.

steps.phase: Choose assignment, analysis, and conclusion policies
steps.title: Keep assignment stable across sessions
steps.content: Consistent hashing is a supplied hint and fits deterministic bucketing by a stable subject key. Version the assignment inputs with the experiment configuration so repeated requests use the same assignment while that configuration is active.

decision.question: How should the router preserve a user's experiment assignment across sessions?
decision.chosen: Use consistent hashing over a stable experiment subject key with a versioned allocation configuration.
decision.chosenReason: A deterministic subject-based assignment is repeatable across sessions and can be recorded with the experiment and configuration version.

alternatives.option: Choose a variant independently for each request
alternatives.tradeoff: It can move one user between variants and makes outcome attribution inconsistent across sessions.

alternatives.option: Store a mutable assignment for every request in the serving path
alternatives.tradeoff: It adds a state lookup to each routing decision and needs explicit consistency behavior during configuration changes.

steps.phase: Choose assignment, analysis, and conclusion policies
steps.title: Make experiment interactions visible to analysis
steps.content: Experiments that affect overlapping users or model behavior can interact. Record their exposure and interaction grouping and analyze compatible combinations explicitly; do not assume each experiment's result is independent when the brief requires handling interaction effects.

decision.question: How should simultaneous experiments be represented when their effects can interact?
decision.chosen: Record experiment exposure and interaction metadata, then include the relevant overlap in the analysis plan.
decision.chosenReason: The analysis needs to distinguish a variant effect from an effect caused by another concurrent experiment.

alternatives.tradeoff: This is simpler but can misattribute outcomes when experiments interact.
This avoids some overlaps but the brief does not require that policy and it limits concurrent experiment design.

steps.phase: Choose assignment, analysis, and conclusion policies
steps.title: Choose a statistical plan before reading outcomes
steps.content: The supplied constraint is statistical significance at p < 0.05. Define the test and stopping behavior before interpreting results. Sequential testing is a supplied hint for early stopping; CUPED is a supplied variance-reduction hint. The brief does not provide an effect-size threshold, sample-size target, metric variance, or test-specific stopping boundary, so obtain those inputs instead of inventing them.

decision.question: How should the framework evaluate an A/B experiment without changing the supplied significance criterion?
decision.chosen: Persist a preselected statistical plan, evaluate the stated p < 0.05 criterion under that plan, and use sequential testing or CUPED only when their assumptions and analysis policy are specified.
decision.chosenReason: A declared plan keeps the supplied threshold interpretable and prevents optional stopping or variance adjustment from being applied without an agreed method.

alternatives.option: Repeatedly inspect a fixed-horizon p-value and stop when it crosses the threshold
alternatives.tradeoff: Repeated unadjusted looks can change the false-positive behavior of the test.

alternatives.option: Use a Bayesian conclusion for every experiment
alternatives.tradeoff: Bayesian methods are a supplied hint, but the brief's p-value constraint still needs an explicit role or an agreed experiment-specific policy.

steps.phase: Choose assignment, analysis, and conclusion policies
steps.title: Reevaluate corrected metrics and novelty effects
steps.content: The live constraint explicitly calls out metric corrections such as novelty effect. Keep enough event identity to replace or revise an earlier metric contribution, mark a result as needing reevaluation while corrections are pending, and update the conclusion when corrected evidence changes it. Do not treat a correction as an additional experiment exposure.

decision.question: What should happen when an experiment metric is corrected after an initial analysis?
decision.chosen: Reconcile the correction against its original exposure and metric identity, then rerun the configured analysis and refresh conclusion state.
decision.chosenReason: A correction changes the evidence for an existing experiment and should not be counted as a new exposure or silently leave a stale conclusion active.

alternatives.option: Append every correction as a new metric observation
alternatives.tradeoff: This can double-count evidence and distort the experiment result.

alternatives.option: Ignore corrections after the first conclusion
alternatives.tradeoff: This leaves the automated decision based on evidence the brief says the system must correct.

steps.phase: Choose assignment, analysis, and conclusion policies
steps.title: Keep bandit allocation distinct from fixed A/B allocation
steps.content: Support multi-armed bandit experiments as a separate allocation mode. The analysis engine may publish adaptive allocation updates through versioned feature flags, while the experiment record retains the policy and assignment history. Bayesian methods are one supplied candidate for faster conclusion; choose them only under an explicit experiment policy and keep their interpretation distinct from the p < 0.05 constraint.

decision.question: How should adaptive bandit traffic allocation coexist with statistically rigorous A/B tests?
decision.chosen: Make allocation mode explicit per experiment, record each policy version and assignment, and use a declared evaluation method for that mode.
decision.chosenReason: Bandits adapt allocation while a fixed A/B design holds allocation rules stable; recording the mode and changes keeps assignment and outcome evidence interpretable.

alternatives.option: Use adaptive allocation for every experiment
alternatives.tradeoff: It can improve allocation decisions but does not by itself satisfy every fixed-design statistical analysis.

alternatives.option: Use only fixed allocation and omit bandits
alternatives.tradeoff: It avoids adaptive-policy complexity but fails the explicit bandit support requirement.

steps.phase: Choose assignment, analysis, and conclusion policies
steps.title: Automate conclusions with evidence and correction state
steps.content: Automate the conclusion decision from the recorded experiment policy, current metric evidence, interaction context, and correction state. Keep the decision traceable and eligible for reevaluation when metrics change. The brief asks for experiment conclusions; it does not specify automatic model promotion, rollback, or a winning-effect threshold.

decision.question: What should the automated experiment conclusion represent?
decision.chosen: A policy-backed status with the evidence and configuration version used, and a reevaluation state when corrected metrics arrive.
decision.chosenReason: This automates the requested experiment decision while preserving the distinction between a measured conclusion and an unspecified deployment action.

alternatives.option: Promote a model automatically as soon as a result is significant
alternatives.tradeoff: The brief does not define promotion criteria or authorize model deployment as part of experiment conclusion.

alternatives.option: Require an operator to calculate every conclusion manually
alternatives.tradeoff: This avoids automated policy but does not meet the requirement to automate experiment conclusion decisions.

steps.phase: Choose assignment, analysis, and conclusion policies
steps.title: Use holdbacks and interleaving only for fitting questions
steps.content: Holdback groups can measure longer-term effects, and interleaving can compare ranking models; both are supplied hints, not mandatory modes for every model experiment. Add the relevant design only when the product question and outcome instrumentation support it, and preserve its assignment and metric definition in the experiment record.

decision.question: Should every model experiment use a holdback group or interleaving?
decision.chosen: Treat both as optional experiment designs selected when they answer the stated evaluation question.
decision.chosenReason: The live brief supplies these techniques as hints but does not make either a universal requirement.

alternatives.option: Apply both methods to every experiment
alternatives.tradeoff: That would impose designs that may not fit the metric or model comparison being evaluated.
That would discard the supplied long-term measurement and ranking-comparison techniques.

steps.phase: Choose assignment, analysis, and conclusion policies
steps.title: Measure the routing latency constraint
steps.content: Validate the serving-path target at the router boundary, including flag lookup, stable assignment, and variant dispatch. This is a target from the live brief, not a measured result in this draft.

scaleTrigger.action: Measure routing latency through the selected configuration and variant-dispatch path, then keep experiment analysis off that synchronous path.
scaleTrigger.impact: A missed target calls for examining routing work and configuration delivery before changing the experiment's statistical policy.

steps.phase: Choose assignment, analysis, and conclusion policies
steps.title: Check the supplied significance criterion
steps.content: Evaluate statistical evidence under the experiment's predeclared test plan and the live p-value criterion. Do not treat a computed p-value as a complete conclusion when metric corrections or interaction effects remain unresolved.

scaleTrigger.action: Apply the declared test and stopping policy to the current corrected outcome evidence.
scaleTrigger.impact: The conclusion must reflect the experiment's analysis design and current evidence state.

steps.phase: Choose assignment, analysis, and conclusion policies
steps.title: Validate concurrent experiment support
steps.content: Exercise concurrent experiment definitions, assignment, event attribution, and analysis together against the stated capacity constraint. This draft sets no additional concurrency or request-volume target.

scaleTrigger.action: Validate that the registry, configuration snapshots, router, event pipeline, and analysis preserve each experiment's identity under concurrent operation.
scaleTrigger.impact: Concurrency pressure must not mix assignments, metric definitions, interaction context, or conclusion state across experiments.

steps.phase: Apply reviewer-critical policies to the existing nodes
steps.title: Register the test plan and interaction layer
steps.content: Apply this design decision to the existing Experiment Registry. Before launch, persist the primary metric, outcome type, hypothesis, comparison family, sample-size/power inputs, stopping plan, and interaction layer. Reject overlapping assignments that conflict within one layer; allow independent layers to run concurrently. The live brief supplies 50+ concurrent experiments but not a sample-size target or a specific statistical policy, so make those explicit inputs rather than invented guarantees.

properties.purpose: Pre-register variants, randomization unit, primary metrics/outcome types, hypothesis and comparison family, power/sample-size inputs, test family/stopping plan, alpha policy, and interaction layer or mutual-exclusion group. Reject conflicting simultaneous assignments within a layer while permitting independent layers to run concurrently. Publish one versioned experiment definition to routing and analysis so both use the same policy.

steps.phase: Apply reviewer-critical policies to the existing nodes
steps.title: Keep routing sticky and independent of analysis
steps.content: Apply this decision to the existing Experiment Traffic Router. Use the local atomic snapshot to resolve layer eligibility and hash a stable subject key with experiment ID and assignment epoch; persist the first variant assignment so later bandit weight changes do not move an enrolled subject. During a config outage, keep the last-known-good snapshot. Measure the supplied sub-5ms target at this serving boundary; never synchronously wait for metrics or conclusions.

properties.purpose: Meet the supplied sub-5ms routing target with an in-memory atomic last-known-good snapshot. Resolve layer/mutual-exclusion eligibility, hash stable subject key plus experiment ID and assignment epoch, and persist each subject's initial variant so later config or bandit-weight revisions do not move an enrolled subject. Do not call registry, analysis, or storage synchronously on the inference path.

steps.phase: Apply reviewer-critical policies to the existing nodes
steps.title: Publish an atomic versioned routing snapshot
steps.content: Apply this decision to the existing Versioned Experiment and Feature Flags node. A snapshot includes variant weights, stable assignment epoch, layer and mutual-exclusion rules, and experiment-plan version. Validate it before atomic publication; routers retain the last-known-good snapshot on invalid or unavailable updates and record the version used for each decision.

properties.purpose: Publish atomically validated, versioned variant weights, assignment epoch, layer/mutual-exclusion rules, and experiment-plan version. Routers record the snapshot version and retain a local last-known-good copy if publication is invalid or the control plane is unavailable; new weights do not rewrite persisted assignments for enrolled subjects.

steps.phase: Apply reviewer-critical policies to the existing nodes
steps.title: Give assignments, exposures, and corrections stable identities
steps.content: Apply this event contract to the existing Experiment Event Stream. Keep the assignment and actual model exposure as different event types; every outcome must point to its original exposure and carry a revision so corrections update evidence instead of inflating sample counts.

properties.purpose: Durably record distinct assignment and actual-exposure events plus outcomes/corrections. Include immutable event_id, exposure_id, experiment_id, variant_id, pseudonymous subject hash, config/test-plan version, event time, metric_id, and correction revision; do not count an assignment as proof of actual model exposure.

steps.phase: Apply reviewer-critical policies to the existing nodes
steps.title: Make metric correction processing idempotent
steps.content: Apply these semantics to the existing Outcome and Correction Processor. Deduplicate at-least-once deliveries; join to the original exposure; upsert a newer correction revision rather than append it as another observation; and publish a settled-through watermark. Results remain provisional while relevant corrections are unresolved.

properties.purpose: Deduplicate at-least-once records by event_id and join outcomes to the original exposure using exposure_id, experiment_id, variant_id, and metric_id. Idempotently upsert correction revisions instead of adding observations, recompute affected aggregates, and emit a settled-through watermark and correction status before final inference.

steps.phase: Apply reviewer-critical policies to the existing nodes
steps.title: Operationalize the p<0.05 analysis policy
steps.content: Apply the pre-registered plan to the existing Experiment Analysis and Decision Engine. Use two-sided Welch tests for continuous outcomes and two-proportion tests for binary outcomes; apply Holm correction across declared primary comparisons. For planned interim looks, use an O'Brien-Fleming alpha-spending boundary with family-wise alpha at 0.05—not repeated unadjusted peeking. Include declared interaction terms or restrict inference to compatible layers, and do not issue a final claim while metric corrections are unresolved. Bandit posterior decisions remain distinct from p-value conclusions.

properties.purpose: On settled exposure/outcome evidence, use two-sided Welch tests for continuous outcomes and two-proportion tests for binary outcomes, with Holm adjustment across declared primary comparisons. Use O'Brien-Fleming alpha-spending for preplanned sequential looks so family-wise alpha remains 0.05; never stop on repeated unadjusted p-values. Include declared interaction terms or analyze only compatible layers; block final inference while corrections remain unresolved. Keep Bayesian bandit allocation/posterior decisions separate from p<0.05 A/B conclusions and persist method/version/evidence.

steps.phase: Apply reviewer-critical policies to the existing nodes
steps.title: Make results auditable and correction-aware
steps.content: Apply this reporting contract to the existing Experiment Results Store. Preserve the exact inputs, analysis policy version, correction watermark, estimates, confidence intervals, raw/adjusted p-values, sample counts, and conclusion status so a dashboard explains why a result is significant, inconclusive, or still awaiting corrected data.

properties.purpose: Persist estimates, confidence intervals, sample counts, raw and Holm-adjusted p-values, test family/plan version, config/assignment version, interaction policy, corrected-data watermark, and conclusion rationale. Report significant, inconclusive, and awaiting-correction states separately so each dashboard result is reproducible from its evidence.

steps.phase: Harden access, recovery, and data lifecycle
steps.title: Enforce access policy at the control API
steps.content: Apply authorization at the API boundary, not only in the console. Authenticate operators with the organization's identity provider; authorize tenant-scoped experiment creation, model-selection changes, and report reads by role; rate-limit mutations; and audit actor, scope, before/after config version, and outcome. These are explicit design choices because the brief does not prescribe an identity provider or role matrix.

properties.purpose: Validate experiment lifecycle and model-selection changes, then publish versioned configuration through the control plane. Enforce authenticated, tenant-scoped role authorization for experiment creation, configuration mutation, and report access; rate-limit control mutations and write an immutable audit record with actor, tenant, action, config version, and outcome. Provider and role names remain deployment decisions.

steps.phase: Harden access, recovery, and data lifecycle
steps.title: Treat the console as an untrusted client
steps.content: Show only tenant-authorized experiments and reports in the console, but never treat UI hiding as the security boundary. Every request is re-authorized by the control API, and pseudonymous subject identifiers are not exposed in ordinary dashboards.

properties.purpose: Create and inspect ML model experiments, feature-flag selections, analysis state, dashboards, and reports. Present tenant-scoped, role-authorized views; treat the console as an untrusted client because the control API re-authorizes every operation, and omit pseudonymous subject identifiers from ordinary dashboards.

steps.phase: Harden access, recovery, and data lifecycle
steps.title: Provide a durable assignment-recovery feed
steps.content: Use a compacted, keyed view of assignment events for asynchronous cache reconstruction after a router restart. This recovery consumer is separate from the inference path and must not add a synchronous event-store read to routing.

connection.label: Assignment recovery feed
connection.description: Replay the compacted assignment ledger asynchronously to rebuild the router's local sticky-assignment cache after restart; never block the sub-5ms request path on this feed.

steps.phase: Harden access, recovery, and data lifecycle
steps.title: Recover sticky assignments without a hot-path lookup
steps.content: Keep the active assignment epoch immutable for enrolled subjects. Persist assignment events under tenant, experiment, and pseudonymous subject keys; rebuild the local cache from the recovery feed asynchronously after restart, and do not synchronously query storage during inference. Hold the last-known-good config while recovery catches up, and expose readiness/recovery lag for operators.

properties.purpose: Meet the supplied sub-5ms routing target with an in-memory atomic last-known-good snapshot. Resolve layer/mutual-exclusion eligibility, hash a stable subject key plus experiment ID and immutable assignment epoch, and preserve each enrolled subject's initial variant across bandit-weight revisions. Persist assignment events keyed by tenant, experiment, and pseudonymous subject; rebuild the local sticky-assignment cache asynchronously from the compacted recovery feed after restart, never by a synchronous inference-path lookup. Expose recovery lag/readiness and retain the last-known-good config while the cache catches up.

steps.phase: Harden access, recovery, and data lifecycle
steps.title: Bound event storage with a correction-aware lifecycle
steps.content: Set an owner-approved retention policy rather than implying unlimited storage. Partition and compact the event stream; keep raw assignment, exposure, outcome, and correction records through the agreed lateness/correction window; then archive or expire them according to tenant and compliance policy. Minimize identifying data and retain the keyed assignment view only as long as sticky-assignment recovery requires it.

properties.purpose: Durably record distinct assignment and actual-exposure events plus outcomes/corrections with immutable event_id, exposure_id, experiment_id, variant_id, pseudonymous subject hash, config/test-plan version, event time, metric_id, and correction revision. Partition and compact records; preserve raw evidence through the owner-approved lateness/correction window, then archive or expire by tenant/compliance retention policy. Minimize identifiers and retain keyed assignment history only as long as recovery requires.

steps.phase: Harden access, recovery, and data lifecycle
steps.title: Retain reproducible outcomes under an explicit policy
steps.content: Keep result retention separate from raw-event retention. Retain the compact analysis evidence needed to reproduce a reported conclusion, enforce tenant-scoped access, and apply the owner-approved compliance lifecycle to detailed evidence and aggregates; do not delete results while corrections or an audit hold remain unresolved.

properties.purpose: Persist estimates, confidence intervals, sample counts, raw and Holm-adjusted p-values, test family/plan version, config/assignment version, interaction policy, corrected-data watermark, and conclusion rationale. Report significant, inconclusive, and awaiting-correction states separately so results are reproducible; enforce tenant-scoped reads and apply owner-approved retention/archival policy without expiring unresolved corrections or audit-held evidence.

steps.phase: Review the local architecture draft
steps.title: Confirm assumptions before implementation
steps.content: This reference architecture connects 12 catalog-backed components across 22 relationships and maps the eight requirements and five constraints to explicit actions. Confirm the workload envelope, identity and tenant-role integration, correction window, and owner-approved retention policy before implementation. The sub-5ms routing target and p<0.05 threshold are stated design goals, not measured guarantees; validate them with production-like traffic and the chosen statistical plan. The assignment-recovery feed is asynchronous and does not add a storage lookup to the inference path.
